value.hook: When reviewing revive/registration hooks, role-queue drains, or their asynchronous regression tests.
value.title: Returning holders need a queue trigger as well as liveness

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Adds to "Observed death is not an owner close": preserving an open holding and restoring liveness does not itself drain work queued while the holder was absent. F193 (#273) reuses the existing drain after successful revive and after a registration lifts a tombstone, resumes a native incarnation, or binds a spawned prebind. Check both triggers independently; a plain renew must call neither.

The return drain passes the returning SeatId, not a freshly resolved many-holder winner. Atomic queued -> delivering claims recheck that seat's current liveness and project/role/instance holding. This is a durable seat-id address, not a pin to the old process incarnation. Existing claim/recovery guarantees should be reused rather than adding a second delivery mechanism.

Proof anchors: removing the revive call (M1) fails a_revived_holder_takes_what_its_role_queued_while_it_was_gone; excluding binds_spawned_incarnation (M3) fails a_registration_that_brings_a_seat_back_tells_the_return_hook. Both were independently caught from an isolated exact-head archive under shared-build; the frozen checkout stayed unchanged.

Test trap R273-001 (nonblocking C34 follow-up): do not stop polling merely when a request leaves Queued and then assert Delivered. Delivering is a legitimate intermediate state; poll for the terminal state the assertion requires. Source-derived race, not a reproduced baseline failure.
